---
title: "minipivot"
---





The purpose of **minipivot** is to provide a zero-dependency
reimplementation of two functions from the
[**tidyr**](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/) package: `pivot_longer()`
and `pivot_wider()`. Together they reshape a data frame between "long"
and "wide" layouts. The [README](https://github.com/djnavarro/minis/tree/main/minipivot)
provides scope notes; this page walks through both functions on a
small toy data frame, including the column-selection styles
`.pivot_longer()` supports and what happens when `.pivot_wider()` is
asked to spread duplicate rows into one cell.

## Functions

The [**minipivot.R**](https://github.com/djnavarro/minis/blob/main/minipivot/minipivot.R)
script supplies two core functions:

- `.pivot_longer(.data, cols, names_to = "name", values_to = "value")`
  is used to melt `cols` into two new columns holding the pivoted
  column names and their values.
- `.pivot_wider(.data, names_from, values_from, values_fill = NULL)`
  is used to spread the unique values of `names_from` into new
  columns, filled from `values_from`.

It contains no internal helpers.

## A minimal data set



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fish <- data.frame(
  location = c("lake", "lake", "sea", "sea"),
  species  = c("trout", "bass", "trout", "bass"),
  count    = c(5, 3, 7, 2)
)
fish
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  location species count
1     lake   trout     5
2     lake    bass     3
3      sea   trout     7
4      sea    bass     2
```


:::
:::



## Wide to long

The `.pivot_longer()` function needs to know which columns to pivot.
Here, `count` is the only column with values to melt, and
`location`/`species` come along for the ride as id columns:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
.pivot_longer(fish, count, names_to = "metric", values_to = "n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  location species metric n
1     lake   trout  count 5
2     lake    bass  count 3
3      sea   trout  count 7
4      sea    bass  count 2
```


:::
:::



## Long to wide

The `.pivot_wider()` function spreads `species`'s unique values
(`trout`/`bass`) into new columns, filled from `count`. There's no
`id_cols` argument to set -- every column other than
`names_from`/`values_from` (`location`, here) is treated as an id
column automatically:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
wide <- .pivot_wider(fish, names_from = "species", values_from = "count")
wide
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  location trout bass
1     lake     5    3
2      sea     7    2
```


:::
:::



## Round-tripping

Pivoting the wide result back out reproduces the original long data
(row order aside, since `.pivot_wider()` reorders rows by id column):



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
.pivot_longer(wide, c(trout, bass), names_to = "species", values_to = "count")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  location species count
1     lake   trout     5
2     lake    bass     3
3      sea   trout     7
4      sea    bass     2
```


:::
:::



## Selecting `cols` a few different ways

The `cols` argument to `.pivot_longer()` accepts more than just a
single bare name. Bare names combined with `c(...)`, a plain character
vector, and a negated `-c(...)` ("every column except these") all
agree, since `trout`/`bass` are the only two columns not already used
as an id column above:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
identical(
  .pivot_longer(wide, c(trout, bass)),
  .pivot_longer(wide, c("trout", "bass"))
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] TRUE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
identical(
  .pivot_longer(wide, c(trout, bass)),
  .pivot_longer(wide, -location)
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] TRUE
```


:::
:::



There is no tidyselect-style `starts_with()`/`everything()` support --
just bare names, `c(...)`, character/numeric vectors, and unary `-`
negation.

## Missing combinations: `values_fill`

Dropping a row before widening leaves a combination unrepresented --
`sea`/`bass` is missing below, so it comes back as `NA` by default:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
.pivot_wider(fish[-4, ], names_from = "species", values_from = "count")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  location trout bass
1     lake     5    3
2      sea     7   NA
```


:::
:::



The `values_fill` argument supplies a value to use instead:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
.pivot_wider(fish[-4, ], names_from = "species", values_from = "count", values_fill = 0)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  location trout bass
1     lake     5    3
2      sea     7    0
```


:::
:::



## Duplicate combinations are an error, not a list-column

Real `tidyr::pivot_wider()` handles a duplicate `names_from`/id
combination by warning and packing the extra values into a
list-column. This mini has no list-column support (matching
[**minitable**](../minitable/)'s scope), so the same situation is a
hard error instead:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dup <- rbind(fish, data.frame(location = "lake", species = "trout", count = 99))
.pivot_wider(dup, names_from = "species", values_from = "count")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error}

```
Error in `.pivot_wider()`:
! .pivot_wider(): `names_from`/id-column combination is not unique (duplicate rows would need to be aggregated); this mini does not implement a `values_fn`-style aggregation step.
```


:::
:::
